  "parent": {
    "title": "Spec: Workshop venue autocomplete and directions",
    "description": "## Problem Statement

Attendees need to reach the right physical Venue from their Calendar Invitation and workshop page. A short venue label can be recognizable to staff without giving an attendee enough information to navigate. Re-entering addresses or guessing which similarly named Google result is correct risks sending people to the wrong place.

Staff need help finding a destination without making Google availability a condition of scheduling. Existing upcoming workshops also need reviewed destination details, including regular Workshops whose normal editing window has closed.

## Solution

Add optional Google venue autocomplete to regular Workshop create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule. Keep the existing short venue label separate from the destination. Staff can select a Google result or enter an address manually, with an optional manually supplied Maps link. Suggestions favour Dublin without excluding other locations.

Show directions on existing attendee-facing workshop pages and populate Calendar's native location field with the destination's recognizable name/address. Extend the existing Calendar integration rather than adding links to event descriptions or introducing another delivery path.

Provide a one-off, reviewed preview/apply backfill for existing upcoming workshops. Enriching the same Venue preserves the label and schedule, uses normal Calendar attendee updates and sends no separate workshop-rescheduled email. Moving a published Workshop to another physical Venue is not authorized by this exception.

This is a specification for later work. It authorizes no implementation, Google provisioning, production activation or production backfill.

## User Stories

### Selecting and maintaining a Venue

 1. As a regular Workshop coordinator, I want venue suggestions when creating a Workshop, so that I can choose a destination attendees can find.
 2. As a regular Workshop coordinator, I want the same input when editing a Workshop, so that I can maintain destination details through the permitted editing workflow.
 3. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want venue suggestions when scheduling, so that prospective members receive a useful destination.
 4. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want the same input when rescheduling, so that destination details follow the workshop's permitted changes.
 5. As a coordinator scheduling several Beginners' Workshops together, I want the shared Venue choice applied to each scheduled date, so that I do not repeat the same selection.
 6. As a coordinator, I want the short venue label kept separate from the full destination, so that existing concise workshop and email copy remains useful.
 7. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want the existing 80-character venue-label limit preserved, so that adding an address cannot break Intake Emails.
 8. As a coordinator, I want to see the selected destination's identifying name/address before saving, so that I can distinguish similarly named places.
 9. As a coordinator, I want suggestions biased toward Dublin, so that likely local destinations are easy to find.
10. As a coordinator, I want to select a destination outside Dublin, so that the bias does not become a geographical restriction.
11. As a coordinator, I want to enter a Venue and address manually, so that an unlisted place remains usable.
12. As a coordinator, I want to save manually when Google fails or is unconfigured, so that scheduling does not depend on a mapping service.
13. As a coordinator, I want to supply a Maps link manually, so that I can identify a useful destination when autocomplete has no suitable result.
14. As a coordinator, I want the manual Maps link to be optional, so that a workshop does not require a mapping-service listing.
15. As a coordinator, I want to replace or clear an optional destination without losing the short label, so that I can correct destination details deliberately.
16. As a coordinator, I want manual edits to a selected destination not to retain an unrelated Place identity or link, so that attendees are not directed to a stale selection.
17. As a coordinator, I want unrelated edits to preserve the saved destination, so that editing workshop copy does not remove directions.
18. As a keyboard user, I want to search, inspect, choose and dismiss suggestions without a pointer, so that I can use the whole form accessibly.
19. As a screen-reader user, I want labelled controls and understandable suggestion, loading, empty and failure states, so that I know what the destination input is doing.
20. As a coordinator, I want field errors and entered values preserved after a failed submission, so that I can correct the form without starting again.
21. As a coordinator, I want selecting a suggestion not to submit the entire form unexpectedly, so that I remain in control of saving the workshop.
22. As a coordinator, I want only the latest search's suggestions shown, so that a slow earlier response cannot replace my current results or chosen destination.
23. As a coordinator, I want venue entry to work on a phone, so that scheduling and corrections do not require a desktop.

### Attendee directions

24. As a member attending a regular Workshop, I want a directions link on the workshop page, so that I can plan my journey.
25. As an external regular Workshop attendee, I want directions on the existing attendee-facing workshop surface, so that navigation is not limited to members.
26. As a Beginners' Workshop attendee, I want directions on my existing workshop-place page, so that I can find the Venue without another public listing.
27. As an attendee, I want the familiar short label and useful destination details together, so that I can connect the workshop's wording to the place on Maps.
28. As an attendee, I want a manually supplied destination to work as well as a Google-selected one, so that the staff's fallback remains useful to me.
29. As an attendee, I want older workshops without destination details to retain their label, so that introducing this feature does not break existing pages.
30. As an attendee, I want links to use safe mapping destinations, so that venue entry cannot turn my workshop page into an unsafe link.
31. As a Beginners' Workshop attendee, I want my private Intake link and token excluded from Google requests and navigation referrers, so that asking for directions does not disclose access to my workshop place.
32. As an attendee, I want no embedded map or automatic location-permission request, so that directions stay a lightweight choice.

### Calendar behaviour and existing policies

33. As an attendee, I want the Venue in Calendar's native location field, so that the Calendar UI can present its ordinary location/navigation experience.
34. As an attendee, I want a recognizable name/address rather than a Place ID or an event-description workaround, so that the event is understandable in Calendar.
35. As a committee member, I want the committee event to show the same destination as the attendee event, so that staff and attendees do not rely on conflicting location information.
36. As an attendee, I want a destination update to retain the existing event and my RSVP, so that enrichment does not create duplicate invitations or reset my response.
37. As an attendee, I want meaningful destination changes to use Calendar's normal update mechanism, so that I can notice the updated details.
38. As an attendee, I want unchanged reconciliation to remain silent, so that repeated background work does not send redundant updates.
39. As an attendee, I want existing workshop emails to remain unchanged, so that directions supplement the current communication workflow.
40. As a coordinator, I want same-Venue enrichment to avoid a separate workshop-rescheduled email, so that additional address detail is not announced as a change of plan.
41. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want an actual reschedule to keep its existing deadlines, history and email policies, so that autocomplete does not redefine rescheduling.
42. As a regular Workshop coordinator, I want published-Workshop editing restrictions preserved, so that this feature does not become a general relocation or rescheduling facility.
43. As an attendee, I want a Google outage not to undo a saved workshop or confirmed place, so that Calendar remains a projection rather than booking authority.
44. As an attendee, I want payment, Registration, Intake, refund and capacity rules unchanged, so that adding directions has no effect on my place.
45. As an attendee, I want private tokens, roster details and payment or medical information excluded from venue lookup and Calendar location content, so that navigation does not broaden disclosure.
46. As an attendee, I want past Calendar details left unchanged by venue enrichment, so that historical events retain their recorded meaning.

### Reviewed upcoming-workshop backfill

47. As a club operator, I want to map existing venue text to a deliberately reviewed destination, so that existing upcoming workshops can receive useful directions.
48. As a reviewer, I want a preview of every affected workshop and its before/after destination, so that I can inspect the complete scope before applying anything.
49. As a reviewer, I want the preview to distinguish regular and Beginners' Workshops even when their IDs or labels match, so that I know exactly which records will change.
50. As a reviewer, I want ambiguous or unmatched venues left unchanged and reported, so that a first search result is never mistaken for an approved destination.
51. As a reviewer, I want multiple workshops with the same venue text visible individually, so that a shared label does not hide an incorrect mapping.
52. As a club operator, I want a read-only preview with no source, job or Google mutations, so that reviewing the mapping cannot send attendee updates.
53. As a club operator, I want same-Venue enrichment available for upcoming regular Workshops outside the normal edit window, so that existing attendees are not excluded from this improvement.
54. As a reviewer, I want the exception limited to destination enrichment at the same physical Venue, so that it cannot move a published workshop elsewhere.
55. As a club operator, I want apply to recheck each current workshop under its owner's normal locking protocol, so that a stale preview cannot overwrite intervening changes.
56. As a club operator, I want workshops that have started, been cancelled or otherwise become ineligible excluded at apply time, so that an old review cannot change inappropriate records.
57. As a club operator, I want only the reviewed targets applied and changed or newly discovered targets reported for review, so that matching text alone cannot silently expand the operation.
58. As a club operator, I want repeat application of an unchanged mapping to be a no-op, so that retrying does not create redundant writes or Calendar update messages.
59. As a reviewer, I want an apply result listing changed, unchanged and refused targets with reasons, so that I can reconcile the result against the preview.
60. As an attendee of an enriched upcoming workshop, I want its date, time, short label and place unchanged, so that receiving a Calendar update does not imply a different workshop.
61. As a club operator, I want production backfill to require explicit authorization after review, so that publishing this spec cannot trigger changes or emails.

### Provider readiness and verification

62. As a club operator, I want Places configuration handled separately from Calendar OAuth, so that working Calendar credentials are not mistaken for autocomplete readiness.
63. As a club operator, I want required Google attribution and applicable storage/use restrictions respected, so that the feature is operated under the right terms.
64. As a coordinator, I want the native Calendar navigation experience checked on an authorized isolated calendar, so that an accepted API write is not presented as proof of the intended Google Place.
65. As a club operator, I want automated tests to substitute Google and live checks to use synthetic isolated data, so that routine verification cannot send real invitations.
66. As a club operator, I want deployment and venue backfill to preserve the existing Calendar activation gate, so that neither operation silently enables production sending.

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain ownership and contracts

* Extend the existing Venue representation in each source domain: its required short label remains independent of optional destination details. Support Google-selected and manual destinations, with an optional directions URL and only the provider identity/provenance needed by the validated integration. Coordinates are not required. A Google response payload is not the persistence or public API shape.
* Keep Workshop and Beginners' Workshop schemas, tables, commands and read models separate under ADR 0029. Share the domain-neutral input and lookup integration, not either domain's storage or scheduling policy. Each scheduled Beginners' Workshop owns its own saved destination even when several dates were created together.
* Ordinary regular Workshop writes stay with the existing public Workshop operations. General edits are currently planned-only; the published pricing-only exception does not grant venue edits. Preserve that gate and add a narrow, authorized source-owned destination-enrichment operation beside it, rather than broadening the general update request.
* Beginners' Workshop writes stay behind Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.execute/3. Add destination-only enrichment as a distinct command in the existing Schedule family, using its shared protocol/locks and Calendar intent. Do not send it through reschedule_workshop: that path increments reschedule_count, clamps windows, delivers rescheduled Intake Emails and notifies Staff. The schedule/reschedule form may collect destination details, but its source-owned operation must distinguish same-Venue enrichment from a genuine reschedule; frontend suppression of emails is not the rule. Keep genuine rescheduling on its existing command and side effects. Neither source uses a cross-domain writer or direct database maintenance script.
* Use additive, nullable destination storage so legacy rows and existing short-label submissions remain valid. Omitted destination fields preserve existing data on updates; an explicit clear removes optional destination details. Editing a selected destination into a different manual one must replace/clear stale provider identity and derived link consistently.
* Extend each domain's request/read contracts, attendee-safe views and Calendar projection through OpenAPI-first changes under ADR 0003. Update frontend schemas and regenerate the typed client. Keep server-side validation, capability checks, closed projections and the existing problem/field-error rendering authoritative. Preserve the Beginners' Workshop label's 80-character maximum; a full address belongs in destination details, not that label.

### Shared input and provider boundary

* Reuse one domain-neutral autocomplete input across regular create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule. Compose existing UI primitives and preserve field.as-derived remote-form names, form enhancement, field errors and values across rejection. Test actual submitted values, not just a displayed selection.
* Autocomplete assists selection; it is never required for a valid label/manual submission. Support unavailable/unconfigured Google, no suitable results, explicit selection, clear/replacement and optional manual Maps links. A failed lookup must not discard staff-entered values. Bias toward Dublin without a hard geographical restriction or a requirement to obtain the staff member's location.
* Keep Places search and selected-result resolution behind one narrow external lookup boundary with no domain-write authority. Prevent stale search responses from overwriting newer results or a selection. Keep provider payloads and provider-specific failures behind this boundary rather than spreading them through the forms and source contexts.
* Use the existing Req/Req.Test convention for Phoenix-side provider HTTP. Any required browser integration remains behind the same lookup boundary; do not introduce a general venue directory or a second Calendar adapter. Record the supported Places integration/configuration and attribution requirements when the terms gate is resolved.
* Places needs its own API enablement, billing and correctly restricted key configuration. Existing organizer OAuth authorizes Calendar operations, not Places. Keep server credentials out of browser responses, jobs and logs; restrict any intentionally browser-exposed key to its required APIs and authorized origins. Missing Places configuration keeps manual scheduling available.

### Attendee pages and safe navigation

* Add directions to the existing regular Workshop member/external attendee surfaces and the Beginners' Workshop safe Intake page; do not introduce a public Beginners' Workshop listing. Preserve short-label rendering for legacy rows. Use saved destination facts to construct a valid directions link, or the validated optional manual Maps link; do not fabricate a selected Place for an unreviewed label.
* Validate manual directions URLs server-side as supported HTTPS Maps destinations. Reject executable schemes, credentials and unsupported targets; render external links safely. Keep the Intake page's no-referrer policy and use referrer-safe navigation so its credential-bearing URL is not sent to Google.
* Lookup receives only the venue search/selection information it needs. Attendee navigation receives only destination information. Neither operation includes Intake links/tokens, attendee lists or private workshop/payment/profile facts. Participant Calendar descriptions remain absent; committee descriptions retain only the existing protected dashboard link.

### Existing Calendar synchronization

* Extend Dhc.Workshops.calendar_projection/1 and Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.calendar_projection/1 to supply a meaningful native location string from the destination name/address, falling back to the existing label for legacy/manual-label-only rows. Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.Sync already maps projection location into Google's free-form event location field; reuse this protocol for both audiences.
* Calendar location is not a structured Place ID contract. Do not put a Maps link into the description as a substitute for native location. A Place ID, a successful Google API response or matching text alone does not prove the desired native navigation experience.
* Record identifier-only Calendar intent in the same source transaction as the destination change through the existing record_change seam. Google calls remain outside source transactions. Preserve event identities/generations, retained recipients, surviving guest records/RSVPs, source-revision/lease/ETag fencing, bounded retry/repair, privacy cleanup and historical cutoffs.
* A meaningful native-location change uses the existing participant update behaviour, including sendUpdates=all; committee-only mutations keep sendUpdates=none. Unchanged reconciliation remains silent. Do not suppress Google's normal update mechanism to avoid emails, and do not claim email delivery is guaranteed.
* Same-Venue enrichment changes no date/time, deadline, offer round, reschedule counter/history or workshop-rescheduled email. Genuine permitted rescheduling still follows existing source policies and notifications. Preserve <issue id="8fed1cf0-a260-4d9e-b9d5-8def40361d01" label="ALE-437" href="https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-437/calendar-launch-preview-and-explicit-activation" />'s target-bound explicit activation and Sentry failure reporting; do not restore superseded pause/resume, manual recipient repair or Calendar dashboard Notifications. Destination enrichment does not create a new place entitlement or choose another recipient address.

### Reviewed backfill

* Provide operator-style preview/apply for both source kinds, using a one-off reviewed mapping from existing venue text to selected/manual destinations. Resolve and review destinations before preview/apply; neither operation automatically chooses search results. This is not a reusable shared venue registry.
* Preview is read-only and performs no Google calls, source/integration writes or job insertion. List every candidate individually with source kind/ID, label, schedule/status, current and proposed destination, eligibility, no-op/refusal reason and expected Calendar update effect. Report ambiguous/unmatched cases unchanged. Recipient addresses and private Intake credentials are not needed in this artifact.
* Apply accepts only explicitly reviewed targets and verifies expected current source facts under source-owned authorization and locks. Recheck that the start is still in the future and the source remains eligible; refuse/report stale, cancelled, started, changed or unreviewed targets rather than expanding the match set or overwriting new information. Use Club Calendar for Dublin schedule interpretation.
* The narrow exception to the regular Workshop edit window permits only destination enrichment at the same physical Venue. Preserve the short label, date/time and all other source facts. Human review establishes same-Venue correspondence; an ambiguous address or a different physical venue remains unchanged for review. Do not relax the ordinary published-Workshop editor.
* Persist an accepted enrichment and its Calendar intent atomically through each owner's supported operation. Repeated unchanged application is a no-op. Return per-target outcomes so the operator can reconcile applied, unchanged and refused entries and safely obtain a fresh preview when needed.
* While Calendar sending is inactive, keep the source change/intent without Google mutations. While active, use the normal update path and accept that Google may email existing attendees. Code delivery does not apply mappings, activate sending or authorize a production run.

### Technical validation gates

* Before finalizing Google-derived persistence or export, check the applicable Google Places/Maps Platform terms, including EEA-specific terms, attribution, permitted use and field-by-field retention/caching requirements. Record what may be persisted, for how long, and any required refresh/deletion behaviour. Do not assume staff selection removes restrictions on Google-derived data or that all returned details can be stored indefinitely. If the agreed behaviour cannot be supported under the applicable terms, report the blocker rather than silently changing the feature.
* Separately authorized isolated-calendar acceptance must inspect the native location/navigation experience with synthetic destinations and attendees. Verify the recognizable destination in relevant Calendar clients, not just the outbound JSON or HTTP status. If native location does not meet the agreed goal, report that result before adding a description-link workaround or claiming exact Place identity.

## Testing Decisions

The user approved these seams on 6 November 2026. Test observable behaviour at the highest existing boundaries. Assert saved/read values, HTTP contracts, visible links, outbound Google state and intended side effects; do not assert private helper call order or mock away the protocol under test. The only new external substitution boundary is Places lookup.

* **Real form and page journeys:** extend existing regular Workshop create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule browser coverage, plus focused E2E submissions through remote forms to Phoenix. Cover selection, manual-only entry, optional link, unavailable/unconfigured Google, no results, replacing/clearing, unrelated edits, invalid fields/URLs, the 80-character label limit, multiple scheduled dates and data surviving rejection. Cover keyboard selection/dismissal, selection not submitting the form, accessible status/error handling, phone layout and out-of-order responses.
* **Attendee-safe reads and navigation:** exercise existing regular member/external attendee surfaces and the safe Intake page. Assert correct destination/label/link round trips, usable manual directions, legacy fallback and rejection of unsafe URLs. Assert private credentials are absent from Google requests, directions queries and navigation referrers; preserve the Intake no-referrer contract.
* **Source operations and API contracts:** drive existing Workshop public operations and BeginnersWorkshops.execute/3 with real persistence and existing fixtures/fixed clocks. Extend source projection and controller contract/client-parity suites to cover nullable legacy fields, omission versus explicit clear, accepted selected/manual data, field errors and unchanged authorization/edit restrictions. Keep Workshop and Beginners' Workshop storage independent.
* **Backfill as a source-owned operation:** test read-only preview, every affected row, ambiguous/unmatched cases, both source kinds with colliding IDs, exact reviewed target sets, expired edit-window enrichment, and refusal of relocation or unrelated changes. Between preview and apply, exercise changed destinations, rescheduling, cancellation, deletion and crossing the start boundary. Assert current-row rechecks, per-target outcomes, no past writes, idempotent repeat application, no direct source bypass and no Google calls inside source transactions.
* **One existing Calendar protocol seam:** run Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.sync/3 against the existing Req.Test Google/OAuth HTTP substitute after real source changes. Prior art is the regular/Beginners' Workshop synchronization, participant, launch and concurrency suites and their stateful Google HTTP fixture. Assert native location for both audiences, unchanged participant descriptions, protected committee link only, sendUpdates=all for meaningful participant location updates, sendUpdates=none for committee events and silence on repeat synchronization.
* **Enrichment is not rescheduling:** through ordinary writes where permitted and the backfill operations, assert unchanged date/time, place/payment/refund/attendance facts, short label, Beginners' Workshop deadline/offer-round/reschedule state and absence of separate workshop-rescheduled email jobs/log occasions or rescheduled Staff notifications. Keep genuine reschedule email behaviour covered separately. Existing email template content and contracts remain unchanged.
* **Recovery, concurrency and history:** extend existing Calendar behaviour tests where destination changes matter: a source enrichment racing an in-flight sync or RSVP update, ambiguous Google success/read-back, retry and duplicate drivers. Assert convergence to the current destination without a duplicate event, reset RSVP, changed recipient binding or extra update on a no-op. Retain exact event-end detail-update/recreation cutoffs and outstanding cancellation/privacy obligations. Use explicit synchronization, not sleeps.
* **Provider substitution and terms:** substitute autocomplete/result-resolution at the single Places boundary, including success, no match, unavailable, quota/authorization failure and stale-response cases. Exercise real request/response mapping through Req.Test where HTTP runs in Phoenix. Add retention/refresh/attribution checks required by the validated integration; do not allow live Google requests in automated suites or persist unrestricted raw provider responses as fixtures.
* **Prior art and verification:** build on the existing Workshop form journeys, Beginners' Workshop scheduling/rescheduling browser tests and end-time backfill tests, source Calendar projection tests, controller contract tests, Calendar launch preview/apply-style revalidation and participant protocol/concurrency suites. During implementation run affected frontend build, typecheck, lint, unit/browser/E2E tests, Phoenix precommit and API generation/idempotency checks. Review any browser-baseline changes and rerun without update mode. Report unrelated pre-existing failures rather than hiding them.
* **Live acceptance is separate:** obtain explicit authorization for isolated Google resources and synthetic data before checking native Calendar navigation and real attendee updates. Places terms/configuration validation and isolated Calendar evidence are technical gates, not claims already verified by this spec. Production provisioning, activation and backfill each remain separately authorized operations.

## Out of Scope

* Implementing this feature, provisioning Google resources, enabling billing/keys, activating production sending or applying production mappings as part of this specification task.
* A new Calendar delivery engine, a change to the two-calendar topology, broader organizer OAuth permissions or restoration of <issue id="8fed1cf0-a260-4d9e-b9d5-8def40361d01" label="ALE-437" href="https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-437/calendar-launch-preview-and-explicit-activation" />'s removed operational features.
* A general ability to relocate or reschedule published regular Workshops, or any relaxation of ordinary editing restrictions beyond the reviewed same-Venue enrichment operation.
* Changes to existing email templates or additional directions/rescheduled emails for enrichment. Google's existing Calendar update notifications are not suppressed.
* Changes to Registration, Intake, Waitlist, membership Invitation, payment, refund, capacity, attendance, deadline or offer-round semantics.
* An embedded map, mandatory coordinates, geolocation permission, route planning, a shared venue directory, or automatic first-result venue matching.
* Backfilling past/started workshops, silently expanding reviewed target sets, or direct database updates outside the owning domain operations.
* Exporting private Intake links, credentials, rosters, medical/payment facts or additional participant-event descriptions to Google.
* A guarantee of exact Google Place binding from Calendar's free-form location field, guaranteed invitation/update email delivery, or any claim that Google Places is already provisioned.

## Further Notes

* Product scope was confirmed by the user on 6 November 2026 in the venue design. The testing seams above were approved during spec assembly. No product-policy interview remains open. The ready-for-agent label means the later work is specified; it does not override the explicit authorization boundary or technical validation gates.
* Calendar integration is already implemented. Read <issue id="5b0bc8e9-efd7-4873-b1ae-da621757dfa5" label="ALE-429" href="https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-429/spec-workshop-calendar-and-calendar-invitations" /> for the original Calendar contract and <issue id="8fed1cf0-a260-4d9e-b9d5-8def40361d01" label="ALE-437" href="https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-437/calendar-launch-preview-and-explicit-activation" /> for the narrowed current launch/operations scope; <issue id="8fed1cf0-a260-4d9e-b9d5-8def40361d01" label="ALE-437" href="https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-437/calendar-launch-preview-and-explicit-activation" /> supersedes conflicting pause/resume, manual repair and failure-Notification requirements. The repository's current Workshop Calendar integration guide and confirmed venue design provide context; this issue is self-contained and does not assume Google provisioning or a production backfill has happened.
* Provisional effort is 3–5 developer days, excluding Google provisioning and human venue review. Native Calendar behaviour and applicable Places terms may constrain implementation; this estimate is not evidence that either gate is satisfied.

    "title": "Spec: Workshop venue autocomplete and directions",
    "description": "## Problem Statement

Attendees need to reach the right physical Venue from their Calendar Invitation and workshop page. A short venue label can be recognizable to staff without giving an attendee enough information to navigate. Re-entering addresses or guessing which similarly named Google result is correct risks sending people to the wrong place.

Staff need help finding a destination without making Google availability a condition of scheduling. Existing upcoming workshops also need reviewed destination details, including regular Workshops whose normal editing window has closed.

## Solution

Add optional Google venue autocomplete to regular Workshop create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule. Keep the existing short venue label separate from the destination. Staff can select a Google result or enter an address manually, with an optional manually supplied Maps link. Suggestions favour Dublin without excluding other locations.

Show directions on existing attendee-facing workshop pages and populate Calendar's native location field with the destination's recognizable name/address. Extend the existing Calendar integration rather than adding links to event descriptions or introducing another delivery path.

Provide a one-off, reviewed preview/apply backfill for existing upcoming workshops. Enriching the same Venue preserves the label and schedule, uses normal Calendar attendee updates and sends no separate workshop-rescheduled email. Moving a published Workshop to another physical Venue is not authorized by this exception.

This is a specification for later work. It authorizes no implementation, Google provisioning, production activation or production backfill.

## User Stories

### Selecting and maintaining a Venue

 1. As a regular Workshop coordinator, I want venue suggestions when creating a Workshop, so that I can choose a destination attendees can find.
 2. As a regular Workshop coordinator, I want the same input when editing a Workshop, so that I can maintain destination details through the permitted editing workflow.
 3. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want venue suggestions when scheduling, so that prospective members receive a useful destination.
 4. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want the same input when rescheduling, so that destination details follow the workshop's permitted changes.
 5. As a coordinator scheduling several Beginners' Workshops together, I want the shared Venue choice applied to each scheduled date, so that I do not repeat the same selection.
 6. As a coordinator, I want the short venue label kept separate from the full destination, so that existing concise workshop and email copy remains useful.
 7. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want the existing 80-character venue-label limit preserved, so that adding an address cannot break Intake Emails.
 8. As a coordinator, I want to see the selected destination's identifying name/address before saving, so that I can distinguish similarly named places.
 9. As a coordinator, I want suggestions biased toward Dublin, so that likely local destinations are easy to find.
10. As a coordinator, I want to select a destination outside Dublin, so that the bias does not become a geographical restriction.
11. As a coordinator, I want to enter a Venue and address manually, so that an unlisted place remains usable.
12. As a coordinator, I want to save manually when Google fails or is unconfigured, so that scheduling does not depend on a mapping service.
13. As a coordinator, I want to supply a Maps link manually, so that I can identify a useful destination when autocomplete has no suitable result.
14. As a coordinator, I want the manual Maps link to be optional, so that a workshop does not require a mapping-service listing.
15. As a coordinator, I want to replace or clear an optional destination without losing the short label, so that I can correct destination details deliberately.
16. As a coordinator, I want manual edits to a selected destination not to retain an unrelated Place identity or link, so that attendees are not directed to a stale selection.
17. As a coordinator, I want unrelated edits to preserve the saved destination, so that editing workshop copy does not remove directions.
18. As a keyboard user, I want to search, inspect, choose and dismiss suggestions without a pointer, so that I can use the whole form accessibly.
19. As a screen-reader user, I want labelled controls and understandable suggestion, loading, empty and failure states, so that I know what the destination input is doing.
20. As a coordinator, I want field errors and entered values preserved after a failed submission, so that I can correct the form without starting again.
21. As a coordinator, I want selecting a suggestion not to submit the entire form unexpectedly, so that I remain in control of saving the workshop.
22. As a coordinator, I want only the latest search's suggestions shown, so that a slow earlier response cannot replace my current results or chosen destination.
23. As a coordinator, I want venue entry to work on a phone, so that scheduling and corrections do not require a desktop.

### Attendee directions

24. As a member attending a regular Workshop, I want a directions link on the workshop page, so that I can plan my journey.
25. As an external regular Workshop attendee, I want directions on the existing attendee-facing workshop surface, so that navigation is not limited to members.
26. As a Beginners' Workshop attendee, I want directions on my existing workshop-place page, so that I can find the Venue without another public listing.
27. As an attendee, I want the familiar short label and useful destination details together, so that I can connect the workshop's wording to the place on Maps.
28. As an attendee, I want a manually supplied destination to work as well as a Google-selected one, so that the staff's fallback remains useful to me.
29. As an attendee, I want older workshops without destination details to retain their label, so that introducing this feature does not break existing pages.
30. As an attendee, I want links to use safe mapping destinations, so that venue entry cannot turn my workshop page into an unsafe link.
31. As a Beginners' Workshop attendee, I want my private Intake link and token excluded from Google requests and navigation referrers, so that asking for directions does not disclose access to my workshop place.
32. As an attendee, I want no embedded map or automatic location-permission request, so that directions stay a lightweight choice.

### Calendar behaviour and existing policies

33. As an attendee, I want the Venue in Calendar's native location field, so that the Calendar UI can present its ordinary location/navigation experience.
34. As an attendee, I want a recognizable name/address rather than a Place ID or an event-description workaround, so that the event is understandable in Calendar.
35. As a committee member, I want the committee event to show the same destination as the attendee event, so that staff and attendees do not rely on conflicting location information.
36. As an attendee, I want a destination update to retain the existing event and my RSVP, so that enrichment does not create duplicate invitations or reset my response.
37. As an attendee, I want meaningful destination changes to use Calendar's normal update mechanism, so that I can notice the updated details.
38. As an attendee, I want unchanged reconciliation to remain silent, so that repeated background work does not send redundant updates.
39. As an attendee, I want existing workshop emails to remain unchanged, so that directions supplement the current communication workflow.
40. As a coordinator, I want same-Venue enrichment to avoid a separate workshop-rescheduled email, so that additional address detail is not announced as a change of plan.
41. As a Beginners' Workshop coordinator, I want an actual reschedule to keep its existing deadlines, history and email policies, so that autocomplete does not redefine rescheduling.
42. As a regular Workshop coordinator, I want published-Workshop editing restrictions preserved, so that this feature does not become a general relocation or rescheduling facility.
43. As an attendee, I want a Google outage not to undo a saved workshop or confirmed place, so that Calendar remains a projection rather than booking authority.
44. As an attendee, I want payment, Registration, Intake, refund and capacity rules unchanged, so that adding directions has no effect on my place.
45. As an attendee, I want private tokens, roster details and payment or medical information excluded from venue lookup and Calendar location content, so that navigation does not broaden disclosure.
46. As an attendee, I want past Calendar details left unchanged by venue enrichment, so that historical events retain their recorded meaning.

### Reviewed upcoming-workshop backfill

47. As a club operator, I want to map existing venue text to a deliberately reviewed destination, so that existing upcoming workshops can receive useful directions.
48. As a reviewer, I want a preview of every affected workshop and its before/after destination, so that I can inspect the complete scope before applying anything.
49. As a reviewer, I want the preview to distinguish regular and Beginners' Workshops even when their IDs or labels match, so that I know exactly which records will change.
50. As a reviewer, I want ambiguous or unmatched venues left unchanged and reported, so that a first search result is never mistaken for an approved destination.
51. As a reviewer, I want multiple workshops with the same venue text visible individually, so that a shared label does not hide an incorrect mapping.
52. As a club operator, I want a read-only preview with no source, job or Google mutations, so that reviewing the mapping cannot send attendee updates.
53. As a club operator, I want same-Venue enrichment available for upcoming regular Workshops outside the normal edit window, so that existing attendees are not excluded from this improvement.
54. As a reviewer, I want the exception limited to destination enrichment at the same physical Venue, so that it cannot move a published workshop elsewhere.
55. As a club operator, I want apply to recheck each current workshop under its owner's normal locking protocol, so that a stale preview cannot overwrite intervening changes.
56. As a club operator, I want workshops that have started, been cancelled or otherwise become ineligible excluded at apply time, so that an old review cannot change inappropriate records.
57. As a club operator, I want only the reviewed targets applied and changed or newly discovered targets reported for review, so that matching text alone cannot silently expand the operation.
58. As a club operator, I want repeat application of an unchanged mapping to be a no-op, so that retrying does not create redundant writes or Calendar update messages.
59. As a reviewer, I want an apply result listing changed, unchanged and refused targets with reasons, so that I can reconcile the result against the preview.
60. As an attendee of an enriched upcoming workshop, I want its date, time, short label and place unchanged, so that receiving a Calendar update does not imply a different workshop.
61. As a club operator, I want production backfill to require explicit authorization after review, so that publishing this spec cannot trigger changes or emails.

### Provider readiness and verification

62. As a club operator, I want Places configuration handled separately from Calendar OAuth, so that working Calendar credentials are not mistaken for autocomplete readiness.
63. As a club operator, I want required Google attribution and applicable storage/use restrictions respected, so that the feature is operated under the right terms.
64. As a coordinator, I want the native Calendar navigation experience checked on an authorized isolated calendar, so that an accepted API write is not presented as proof of the intended Google Place.
65. As a club operator, I want automated tests to substitute Google and live checks to use synthetic isolated data, so that routine verification cannot send real invitations.
66. As a club operator, I want deployment and venue backfill to preserve the existing Calendar activation gate, so that neither operation silently enables production sending.

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain ownership and contracts

* Extend the existing Venue representation in each source domain: its required short label remains independent of optional destination details. Support Google-selected and manual destinations, with an optional directions URL and only the provider identity/provenance needed by the validated integration. Coordinates are not required. A Google response payload is not the persistence or public API shape.
* Keep Workshop and Beginners' Workshop schemas, tables, commands and read models separate under ADR 0029. Share the domain-neutral input and lookup integration, not either domain's storage or scheduling policy. Each scheduled Beginners' Workshop owns its own saved destination even when several dates were created together.
* Ordinary regular Workshop writes stay with the existing public Workshop operations. General edits are currently planned-only; the published pricing-only exception does not grant venue edits. Preserve that gate and add a narrow, authorized source-owned destination-enrichment operation beside it, rather than broadening the general update request.
* Beginners' Workshop writes stay behind Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.execute/3. Add destination-only enrichment as a distinct command in the existing Schedule family, using its shared protocol/locks and Calendar intent. Do not send it through reschedule_workshop: that path increments reschedule_count, clamps windows, delivers rescheduled Intake Emails and notifies Staff. The schedule/reschedule form may collect destination details, but its source-owned operation must distinguish same-Venue enrichment from a genuine reschedule; frontend suppression of emails is not the rule. Keep genuine rescheduling on its existing command and side effects. Neither source uses a cross-domain writer or direct database maintenance script.
* Use additive, nullable destination storage so legacy rows and existing short-label submissions remain valid. Omitted destination fields preserve existing data on updates; an explicit clear removes optional destination details. Editing a selected destination into a different manual one must replace/clear stale provider identity and derived link consistently.
* Extend each domain's request/read contracts, attendee-safe views and Calendar projection through OpenAPI-first changes under ADR 0003. Update frontend schemas and regenerate the typed client. Keep server-side validation, capability checks, closed projections and the existing problem/field-error rendering authoritative. Preserve the Beginners' Workshop label's 80-character maximum; a full address belongs in destination details, not that label.

### Shared input and provider boundary

* Reuse one domain-neutral autocomplete input across regular create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule. Compose existing UI primitives and preserve field.as-derived remote-form names, form enhancement, field errors and values across rejection. Test actual submitted values, not just a displayed selection.
* Autocomplete assists selection; it is never required for a valid label/manual submission. Support unavailable/unconfigured Google, no suitable results, explicit selection, clear/replacement and optional manual Maps links. A failed lookup must not discard staff-entered values. Bias toward Dublin without a hard geographical restriction or a requirement to obtain the staff member's location.
* Keep Places search and selected-result resolution behind one narrow external lookup boundary with no domain-write authority. Prevent stale search responses from overwriting newer results or a selection. Keep provider payloads and provider-specific failures behind this boundary rather than spreading them through the forms and source contexts.
* Use the existing Req/Req.Test convention for Phoenix-side provider HTTP. Any required browser integration remains behind the same lookup boundary; do not introduce a general venue directory or a second Calendar adapter. Record the supported Places integration/configuration and attribution requirements when the terms gate is resolved.
* Places needs its own API enablement, billing and correctly restricted key configuration. Existing organizer OAuth authorizes Calendar operations, not Places. Keep server credentials out of browser responses, jobs and logs; restrict any intentionally browser-exposed key to its required APIs and authorized origins. Missing Places configuration keeps manual scheduling available.

### Attendee pages and safe navigation

* Add directions to the existing regular Workshop member/external attendee surfaces and the Beginners' Workshop safe Intake page; do not introduce a public Beginners' Workshop listing. Preserve short-label rendering for legacy rows. Use saved destination facts to construct a valid directions link, or the validated optional manual Maps link; do not fabricate a selected Place for an unreviewed label.
* Validate manual directions URLs server-side as supported HTTPS Maps destinations. Reject executable schemes, credentials and unsupported targets; render external links safely. Keep the Intake page's no-referrer policy and use referrer-safe navigation so its credential-bearing URL is not sent to Google.
* Lookup receives only the venue search/selection information it needs. Attendee navigation receives only destination information. Neither operation includes Intake links/tokens, attendee lists or private workshop/payment/profile facts. Participant Calendar descriptions remain absent; committee descriptions retain only the existing protected dashboard link.

### Existing Calendar synchronization

* Extend Dhc.Workshops.calendar_projection/1 and Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.calendar_projection/1 to supply a meaningful native location string from the destination name/address, falling back to the existing label for legacy/manual-label-only rows. Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.Sync already maps projection location into Google's free-form event location field; reuse this protocol for both audiences.
* Calendar location is not a structured Place ID contract. Do not put a Maps link into the description as a substitute for native location. A Place ID, a successful Google API response or matching text alone does not prove the desired native navigation experience.
* Record identifier-only Calendar intent in the same source transaction as the destination change through the existing record_change seam. Google calls remain outside source transactions. Preserve event identities/generations, retained recipients, surviving guest records/RSVPs, source-revision/lease/ETag fencing, bounded retry/repair, privacy cleanup and historical cutoffs.
* A meaningful native-location change uses the existing participant update behaviour, including sendUpdates=all; committee-only mutations keep sendUpdates=none. Unchanged reconciliation remains silent. Do not suppress Google's normal update mechanism to avoid emails, and do not claim email delivery is guaranteed.
* Same-Venue enrichment changes no date/time, deadline, offer round, reschedule counter/history or workshop-rescheduled email. Genuine permitted rescheduling still follows existing source policies and notifications. Preserve <issue id="8fed1cf0-a260-4d9e-b9d5-8def40361d01" label="ALE-437" href="https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-437/calendar-launch-preview-and-explicit-activation" />'s target-bound explicit activation and Sentry failure reporting; do not restore superseded pause/resume, manual recipient repair or Calendar dashboard Notifications. Destination enrichment does not create a new place entitlement or choose another recipient address.

### Reviewed backfill

* Provide operator-style preview/apply for both source kinds, using a one-off reviewed mapping from existing venue text to selected/manual destinations. Resolve and review destinations before preview/apply; neither operation automatically chooses search results. This is not a reusable shared venue registry.
* Preview is read-only and performs no Google calls, source/integration writes or job insertion. List every candidate individually with source kind/ID, label, schedule/status, current and proposed destination, eligibility, no-op/refusal reason and expected Calendar update effect. Report ambiguous/unmatched cases unchanged. Recipient addresses and private Intake credentials are not needed in this artifact.
* Apply accepts only explicitly reviewed targets and verifies expected current source facts under source-owned authorization and locks. Recheck that the start is still in the future and the source remains eligible; refuse/report stale, cancelled, started, changed or unreviewed targets rather than expanding the match set or overwriting new information. Use Club Calendar for Dublin schedule interpretation.
* The narrow exception to the regular Workshop edit window permits only destination enrichment at the same physical Venue. Preserve the short label, date/time and all other source facts. Human review establishes same-Venue correspondence; an ambiguous address or a different physical venue remains unchanged for review. Do not relax the ordinary published-Workshop editor.
* Persist an accepted enrichment and its Calendar intent atomically through each owner's supported operation. Repeated unchanged application is a no-op. Return per-target outcomes so the operator can reconcile applied, unchanged and refused entries and safely obtain a fresh preview when needed.
* While Calendar sending is inactive, keep the source change/intent without Google mutations. While active, use the normal update path and accept that Google may email existing attendees. Code delivery does not apply mappings, activate sending or authorize a production run.

### Technical validation gates

* Before finalizing Google-derived persistence or export, check the applicable Google Places/Maps Platform terms, including EEA-specific terms, attribution, permitted use and field-by-field retention/caching requirements. Record what may be persisted, for how long, and any required refresh/deletion behaviour. Do not assume staff selection removes restrictions on Google-derived data or that all returned details can be stored indefinitely. If the agreed behaviour cannot be supported under the applicable terms, report the blocker rather than silently changing the feature.
* Separately authorized isolated-calendar acceptance must inspect the native location/navigation experience with synthetic destinations and attendees. Verify the recognizable destination in relevant Calendar clients, not just the outbound JSON or HTTP status. If native location does not meet the agreed goal, report that result before adding a description-link workaround or claiming exact Place identity.

## Testing Decisions

The user approved these seams on 6 November 2026. Test observable behaviour at the highest existing boundaries. Assert saved/read values, HTTP contracts, visible links, outbound Google state and intended side effects; do not assert private helper call order or mock away the protocol under test. The only new external substitution boundary is Places lookup.

* **Real form and page journeys:** extend existing regular Workshop create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule browser coverage, plus focused E2E submissions through remote forms to Phoenix. Cover selection, manual-only entry, optional link, unavailable/unconfigured Google, no results, replacing/clearing, unrelated edits, invalid fields/URLs, the 80-character label limit, multiple scheduled dates and data surviving rejection. Cover keyboard selection/dismissal, selection not submitting the form, accessible status/error handling, phone layout and out-of-order responses.
* **Attendee-safe reads and navigation:** exercise existing regular member/external attendee surfaces and the safe Intake page. Assert correct destination/label/link round trips, usable manual directions, legacy fallback and rejection of unsafe URLs. Assert private credentials are absent from Google requests, directions queries and navigation referrers; preserve the Intake no-referrer contract.
* **Source operations and API contracts:** drive existing Workshop public operations and BeginnersWorkshops.execute/3 with real persistence and existing fixtures/fixed clocks. Extend source projection and controller contract/client-parity suites to cover nullable legacy fields, omission versus explicit clear, accepted selected/manual data, field errors and unchanged authorization/edit restrictions. Keep Workshop and Beginners' Workshop storage independent.
* **Backfill as a source-owned operation:** test read-only preview, every affected row, ambiguous/unmatched cases, both source kinds with colliding IDs, exact reviewed target sets, expired edit-window enrichment, and refusal of relocation or unrelated changes. Between preview and apply, exercise changed destinations, rescheduling, cancellation, deletion and crossing the start boundary. Assert current-row rechecks, per-target outcomes, no past writes, idempotent repeat application, no direct source bypass and no Google calls inside source transactions.
* **One existing Calendar protocol seam:** run Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.sync/3 against the existing Req.Test Google/OAuth HTTP substitute after real source changes. Prior art is the regular/Beginners' Workshop synchronization, participant, launch and concurrency suites and their stateful Google HTTP fixture. Assert native location for both audiences, unchanged participant descriptions, protected committee link only, sendUpdates=all for meaningful participant location updates, sendUpdates=none for committee events and silence on repeat synchronization.
* **Enrichment is not rescheduling:** through ordinary writes where permitted and the backfill operations, assert unchanged date/time, place/payment/refund/attendance facts, short label, Beginners' Workshop deadline/offer-round/reschedule state and absence of separate workshop-rescheduled email jobs/log occasions or rescheduled Staff notifications. Keep genuine reschedule email behaviour covered separately. Existing email template content and contracts remain unchanged.
* **Recovery, concurrency and history:** extend existing Calendar behaviour tests where destination changes matter: a source enrichment racing an in-flight sync or RSVP update, ambiguous Google success/read-back, retry and duplicate drivers. Assert convergence to the current destination without a duplicate event, reset RSVP, changed recipient binding or extra update on a no-op. Retain exact event-end detail-update/recreation cutoffs and outstanding cancellation/privacy obligations. Use explicit synchronization, not sleeps.
* **Provider substitution and terms:** substitute autocomplete/result-resolution at the single Places boundary, including success, no match, unavailable, quota/authorization failure and stale-response cases. Exercise real request/response mapping through Req.Test where HTTP runs in Phoenix. Add retention/refresh/attribution checks required by the validated integration; do not allow live Google requests in automated suites or persist unrestricted raw provider responses as fixtures.
* **Prior art and verification:** build on the existing Workshop form journeys, Beginners' Workshop scheduling/rescheduling browser tests and end-time backfill tests, source Calendar projection tests, controller contract tests, Calendar launch preview/apply-style revalidation and participant protocol/concurrency suites. During implementation run affected frontend build, typecheck, lint, unit/browser/E2E tests, Phoenix precommit and API generation/idempotency checks. Review any browser-baseline changes and rerun without update mode. Report unrelated pre-existing failures rather than hiding them.
* **Live acceptance is separate:** obtain explicit authorization for isolated Google resources and synthetic data before checking native Calendar navigation and real attendee updates. Places terms/configuration validation and isolated Calendar evidence are technical gates, not claims already verified by this spec. Production provisioning, activation and backfill each remain separately authorized operations.

## Out of Scope

* Implementing this feature, provisioning Google resources, enabling billing/keys, activating production sending or applying production mappings as part of this specification task.
* A new Calendar delivery engine, a change to the two-calendar topology, broader organizer OAuth permissions or restoration of <issue id="8fed1cf0-a260-4d9e-b9d5-8def40361d01" label="ALE-437" href="https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-437/calendar-launch-preview-and-explicit-activation" />'s removed operational features.
* A general ability to relocate or reschedule published regular Workshops, or any relaxation of ordinary editing restrictions beyond the reviewed same-Venue enrichment operation.
* Changes to existing email templates or additional directions/rescheduled emails for enrichment. Google's existing Calendar update notifications are not suppressed.
* Changes to Registration, Intake, Waitlist, membership Invitation, payment, refund, capacity, attendance, deadline or offer-round semantics.
* An embedded map, mandatory coordinates, geolocation permission, route planning, a shared venue directory, or automatic first-result venue matching.
* Backfilling past/started workshops, silently expanding reviewed target sets, or direct database updates outside the owning domain operations.
* Exporting private Intake links, credentials, rosters, medical/payment facts or additional participant-event descriptions to Google.
* A guarantee of exact Google Place binding from Calendar's free-form location field, guaranteed invitation/update email delivery, or any claim that Google Places is already provisioned.

## Further Notes

* Product scope was confirmed by the user on 6 November 2026 in the venue design. The testing seams above were approved during spec assembly. No product-policy interview remains open. The ready-for-agent label means the later work is specified; it does not override the explicit authorization boundary or technical validation gates.
* Calendar integration is already implemented.
